Meeting header:

-- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um this is Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this; quick intros?
[00:08] Lena: Hi, lena here - head of AI at Catalpa. we're excited to get the inference pipeline integrated.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus bloom, platform engineering - i'll own the infra side and handoffs.
[00:15] Ashley: Ashley, CTO - i'll be on for the first few runbooks and gating.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, compliance - quick questions about logging and audit.
[00:22] Jordan: Perfect. Priya and Evan from our side will run the runbook and the bench respectively. Priya?
[00:27] Priya: Hi - i'll be your CSM, i'll coordinate the onboarding sprints and the ops playbook review.
[00:31] Evan: Evan, SE - i'll run the benchmark and help tune the model and batch settings.
[00:36] Jordan: Cool. High level agenda: confirm success metrics, finalize whether you'll go Hosted or Dedicated for pilot, security checklist (VPC, KMS, SSO), then a quick timing and next steps.
[00:48] Ashley: Quick context - we have a retail recommender that's currently calling an in-house LLM for personalization. we're seeing inconsistent p99 latency at peak and token bill shock. So the goal is consistent < 300ms p95 for short prompts and cost predictability.
[01:05] Jordan: Good, that's helpful. Marcus, what's your current infra footprint and network setup?
[01:09] Marcus: We're on AWS, currently us-west-2. We run our APIs in k8s (EKS) and have a NAT/ingress setup. we can do VPC peering and transit gateway but we'd prefer not to punch holes for managed services unless necessary.
[01:23] Evan: Ok, so Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment are both on the table. Dedicated will give you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; Private gives full control but is heavier ops.
[01:35] Lena: We're leaning Dedicated because we want Redwood-managed infra but isolated from other tenants. also we want KMS integration for key management - we use AWS KMS.
[01:44] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated via a KMS role and you can attach a CMK. we can walk Samir through the encryption flow.
[01:51] Samir: Great, i need to confirm whether logs containing user prompts are stored in plaintext and how long audit logs are retained. SOC 2 reqs.
[01:58] Jordan: Good Q. Data plane: by default we encrypt in transit and at rest; logs are configurable - retention policies can be set per-customer, and we can redact or hash PII at ingestion. we'll share the security docs.
[02:12] Marcus: timeline wise - we want a pilot in 3 weeks, target go/no-go end of april. do you think that's reasonable?
[02:18] Evan: For a basic Dedicated pilot with a single model and a small traffic profile, yes 3 weeks is realistic: provisioning, network peering, initial benchmark. if you want private on-prem it adds more time.
[02:28] Ashley: The main acceptance criteria: p95 <300ms for 8-token prompts at 100 RPS, throughput >= 80 req/s sustained without queueing, and cost per 1k tokens below our current baseline.
[02:40] Evan: we'll capture that in the SOW; i want to call out quantization/latency tradeoffs - smaller quantized models reduce cost but can affect quality. we'll define acceptable regen rates.
[02:51] Jordan: Great. Marcus, can you give us a rough token distribution? at peak what's the typical seq length?
[02:57] Marcus: Most calls are short - 8-40 tokens for the recommender, a small tail of 200 tokens for debug sessions. 95% under 40 tokens.
[03:06] Evan: That helps a lot - we can optimize kernels for short sequences and pick batching strategies. also we have prefix/K-V cache for reuse across sessions which will lower token cost.
[03:16] Marcus: is KV cache persisted across restarts? we have concerns about warm-up.
[03:20] Evan: K-V cache is in-memory per serving instance; we have options for sticky routing to keep KV warmed, and for Dedicated we can tune pool size to reduce cold starts. 
[03:31] Lena: About observability - we need token level cost, per-route latency, distributed traces and a retention of 90 days for traces. can Redwood expose traces to our Splunk?
[03:42] Priya: Yes - Redwood Console supports integrations. we can push traces via OTLP or S3 export. we'll document the setup.
[03:49] Samir: Also can you write the audit log schema? we need to show auditors.
[03:53] Jordan: We'll include sample audit log schema in the security packet. we'll also include SOC2 artifact references.
[03:58] Ashley: Network: we prefer VPC peering over public endpoints. is private-link supported?
[04:03] Evan: We support both VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink for hosted/Dedicated. Private deployment supports direct on-prem install but that's heavier.
[04:13] Marcus: Any special ports or egress rules?
[04:16] Evan: Standard TLS 443 egress for control; for VPC peering you'll need internal ranges. we'll share a network workbook.
[04:23] Jordan: ok, bench plan — Evan will run a 1-hour window mimicking your 95th percentile traffic with the model you pick. we'll attempt a scale test up to your 100 RPS.
[04:33] Evan: i'll need sample prompt sets and a small dataset of example requests (no PII) and the token distribution. also confirm the model family - open Llama variant or a quantized 7B?
[04:45] Lena: We're testing a fine-tuned 7B Llama variant. it's internal; we can share a container or weights via s3.
[04:52] Evan: ok fine. for the pilot we'll test a quantized float16 path and a 4-bit profile to estimate tradeoffs.
[04:59] Marcus: When you say quantization recommendations, do you provide quality regression alerts?
[05:03] Priya: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitors tied to eval prompt sets, we can set up thresholds and regression alerts to Slack or email.
[05:12] Samir: On PII - we need rewrites or redaction at ingestion. can that be an option?
[05:17] Evan: Yes; pre-processing hooks or a middleware layer can redact/hide PII before it reaches the inference plane. we can add a sample pre-hook.
[05:25] Ashley: Billing - will the pilot be usage-based or will we have a short-term reserved capacity?
[05:29] Jordan: For pilots we usually do a time-limited reserved block on Dedicated so you get predictable capacity; billing can be pro-rated and then you can convert to committed reserved capacity if you want.
[05:40] Lena: Pricing - we need per-hour cost for the Dedicated pool and an estimate on token unit cost under your batching/caching recommendations.
[05:46] Jordan: we'll send a detailed pricing spreadsheet. Evan will include assumed batch sizes and cache hit rates.
[05:52] Marcus: Any known limitations with our EKS ingress? we use kube-proxy and envoy.
[05:57] Evan: No big issues; we usually put an ingress-to-redwood-agent in your VPC for routing. envoy is fine, just ensure connection timeout is high enough for long tails.
[06:07] Lena: Does Redwood support function calling / structured output for our observability pipeline?
[06:12] Jordan: Yes, the API supports structured output, function/tool calling, and streaming.
[06:16] Ashley: Ok. security docs - we'll want the SOC2 and penetration testing reports before we sign SOW. can you provide them?
[06:22] Priya: Yes - we'll share SOC2 scope and pen test summary. for the SOW we'll include an appendix for security artifacts and the runbook.
[06:30] Samir: Also looking for retention controls: can token content be configured to not be stored?
[06:35] Jordan: Yes, by default logs are retained for X days but you can opt out of storing prompt content or set PII redaction. we'll surface the exact flags in the security packet.
[06:44] Marcus: ok timeline recap? we want pilot start 3/30, run benchmarks first week, then go/no-go by 4/23.
[06:51] Jordan: That matches our plan. Evan, can you confirm availability week of 3/30?
[06:55] Evan: yes; i'll block time. Marcus - please upload prompt set by 3/23.
[06:59] Marcus: will do.
[07:01] Jordan: Any blockers we haven't covered?
[07:04] Lena: one concern - fallback behavior if Dedicated capacity hits limits: do you have automatic fallback to hosted models?
[07:11] Evan: yes - smart routing supports fallback policies. we can route to a lower-cost, higher-latency compatible variant during capacity spikes, and we'll notify via the console and webhook.
[07:22] Ashley: can we set transparent circuit-breakers so product teams don't see errors?
[07:27] Priya: yep, Redwood supports automatic fallback and can set rate-limiting and graceful degradation policies.
[07:34] Samir: auditors may ask about data location - we need EU/US region controls.
[07:37] Jordan: we support region pinning per-customer; Dedicated pools can be provisioned in specific regions.
[07:44] Marcus: ok. last thing - who owns the runbook review?
[07:48] Priya: i'll host the runbook review and invite your infra and security. i'll put together an initial draft by Friday 3/20.
[07:55] Jordan: Great. quick recap and next steps - Jordan to send pricing + SOW by Tue 3/24, Priya to push runbook draft by Fri 3/20, Marcus to upload prompts by Mon 3/23, Evan to schedule bench for week of 3/30.
[08:12] Lena: Sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:15] Jordan: Thanks - we'll follow up with the packet after the call.
